prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” roofing company for hurricane-rated roof replacement in Miami — the right contractor depends on your exact location, roof type (shingle, tile, metal), budget, and whether you need a homeowner-preferred warranty or a code-compliant commercial system. I can help you find the best fit, but first here’s how to identify a top hurricane‑rated roofer and what to ask.

What to look for (requirements and credentials)
- Miami‑Dade/Florida product approvals: They should use materials with Miami‑Dade County NOA (Notice of Acceptance) or Florida Product Approval for high‑wind regions.  
- Contractor license & insurance: Verify a Florida roofing contractor license and current general liability + workers’ comp insurance. Check DBPR (Florida Dept. of Business & Professional Regulation).  
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, Owens Corning Preferred, or similar — indicates training and access to extended warranties.  
- Hurricane/high‑wind experience: Several completed hurricane‑rated jobs in Miami (ask for photos and references).  
- Written warranties: Ask for both material (manufacturer) and workmanship (contractor) warranties, and get details in writing (term, transferability, exclusions).  
- Local code & permitting: The contractor should pull permits and handle inspections (important in Miami‑Dade).  
- Proven practices: Proper tear‑off vs overlay per code, high‑wind fastening (ring shank nails/screws), deck repair, correct underlayment and flashing, sealed ridges/hips, and hip/ridge design for wind uplift.  
- Reputation: Multiple recent positive reviews on Google/Yelp, and a good BBB rating. Get at least three written estimates.

Questions to ask every roofer
- Do you use Miami‑Dade NOA‑approved products for hurricane zones? Which products and NOA numbers?  
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see the license number and insurance certificate?  
- Do you have manufacturer certification (and will that keep my warranty intact)?  
- Can you provide local references for similar hurricane‑rated projects?  
- Who pulls the permits and manages inspections?  
- What is included in the price (decking, underlayment, ventilation, disposal)? Any exclusions?  
- What are the exact warranties (length, coverage, and transferability)?

Where to verify
- Florida DBPR to confirm contractor license.  
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control/NOA search for approved systems.  
- Manufacturer websites to verify installers’ certification.  
- Google, Yelp, and BBB for recent reviews and complaint history.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated hurricane‑rated roofers near you if you give your Miami zip code, or  
- Provide a short vetted checklist/email script you can send to contractors to compare bids.

Which would you prefer?
